URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/raf-fairford-trump-terror-suspects-arrested-gloucestershire-b3057154.html
The Independent — published 27 September 2026 (PA-sourced). Text via Exa search highlights. Companion piece: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/raf-fairford-bomb-squad-terror-police-b3057158.html (same date), quoted below where marked [B3057158].

US president Donald Trump has said a suspected terror plot against an RAF base used by the US Air Force
was "looking to do big damage". Mr Trump hailed the UK police response, while suggesting authorities
already had the suspects under investigation.

Trump, verbatim: "It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job. We had them under
investigation. They, they were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked
out great." And: "We had them under view for a long time, and we got them."

About 85 households have been evacuated from their homes near RAF Fairford. A major incident was
declared and a large emergency services presence was seen in the area, including a Hazardous Area
Response Team within a 400-metre cordon. Aerial footage showed a bomb disposal robot inspecting three
white vans, two of which had open rear doors. Large black barrels appeared to be scattered around.

[B3057158] "Following the incident, Fairford has been raised to the highest threat level, Delta, while
US airbase Lakenheath in Suffolk is on Charlie alert, the second-highest threat level that can be issued
by the US Department of Defence."
[B3057158] "In July, the British government insisted it 'stands ready 24/7 to defend itself' after Iran
said UK airbases used by the US were considered 'legitimate targets'."
[B3057158] Vicki Evans, Counter Terrorism Policing senior national coordinator: "We are in the early
stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody. As you would expect we are working closely
with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident. We continue to work with
Gloucestershire Police to keep the community safe as we work to gather evidence from the scene. A 400m
cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army's Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit
conduct examinations. As a precaution, around 85 households have been evacuated whilst these
examinations take place."
[B3057158] "Detectives are reported to be keeping an open mind but, according to The Times, one line of
inquiry is whether the incident is linked to Tehran as the base has been used to launch operations
against Iran."
[B3057158] The base hosts the American 501st Combat Support Wing.

REUTERS-ORIGINATED ADDITIONS (wire text seen via Straits Times and Dunya News, NEITHER APPROVED — recorded
here only to log the Reuters wire language; the approved carriers above cover everything used in the brief):
"An Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely, a source familiar with the investigation said,
while a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot were also being looked at."
"Reuters witnesses said security had been increased at other bases used by the US, with armoured vehicles
and soldiers at the gates of RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall in eastern England."
Local councillor Tristan Wilkinson to Reuters: "So there was a specific threat about six weeks ago from
the Iranians on this base. At the time, there was increased surveillance around the area."

NOT USABLE: the PA line that the operation was "not intelligence-led", and Wes Streeting's fringe-event
answer ("I'm not going to comment on the underlying motivations of those who've been arrested today...
it would be irresponsible for me to do so"), were found only in The Standard, which is banned. Needs an
approved carrier before either is published.
